title: Responding vs. reacting
content: A reaction is fast and automatic, driven by that quicker brain pathway, with little conscious thought involved. A response is what happens when there's a small gap between what happens and what you do about it, even a few seconds, giving the slower, more deliberate part of your brain time to catch up. That gap is exactly what skills like breathing or grounding are trying to create: not removing the emotion, but making room for a response instead of a reaction. If you’d like to learn more about those skills I can take you through them.
